A woman engaged in agriculture, raising living organisms for food or raw materials. Generally depicted as wearing a wide-brimmed hat and holding a crop (such as carrots or corn) or a pitchfork.

A person responsible for food preparation wearing a white buttoned chef jacket and toque hat.

Usually shown with either a wooden spoon or a skillet frying an egg, though WhatsApp's design is holding a spatula.

A man responsible for food preparation wearing a white buttoned chef jacket and toque hat.

Usually shown with either a wooden spoon or a skillet frying an egg, though WhatsApp's design is holding a spatula.

A woman responsible for food preparation wearing a white buttoned chef jacket and toque hat.

Usually shown with either a wooden spoon or a skillet frying an egg, though WhatsApp's design is holding a spatula.
A person engaged in the construction, maintenance, or repair of machinery. Depicted wearing overalls and holding a wrench. Frequently also shown wearing a billed cap.
A man engaged in the construction, maintenance, or repair of machinery. Depicted wearing overalls and holding a wrench. Frequently also shown wearing a billed cap.
A woman engaged in the construction, maintenance, or repair of machinery. Depicted wearing overalls and holding a wrench. Frequently also shown wearing a billed cap.
A person working in a factory setting, depicted as wearing overalls and protective headgear while holding an active welding gun.
A man working in a factory setting, depicted as wearing overalls and protective headgear while holding an active welding gun.
A woman working in a factory setting, depicted as wearing overalls and protective headgear while holding an active welding gun.
A person wearing business attire. This may include items such as a shirt, tie, jacket, or headset.
A man wearing business attire. This may include items such as a shirt, tie, jacket, or headset.
A woman wearing business attire. This may include items such as a shirt, blouse, tie, jacket, or headset.

A person who is studying or has expert knowledge of one or more of the natural or physical sciences. Generally depicted wearing safety goggles and a white lab coat while holding a test tube or beaker filled with colorful liquid.

A man who is studying or has expert knowledge of one or more of the natural or physical sciences. Generally depicted wearing safety goggles and a white lab coat while holding a test tube filled with colorful liquid.

A woman who is studying or has expert knowledge of one or more of the natural or physical sciences. Generally depicted wearing safety goggles and a white lab coat while holding a test tube filled with colorful liquid.

A person behind a computer screen, working in the field of technology.

Usually shown working on a laptop, though Google's design appears to be using a desktop computer instead.

A man behind a computer screen, working in the field of technology.

Usually shown working on a laptop, though Google's design previously appeared to be using a desktop computer instead.

The laptop in Apple's design includes the Apple logo, consistent with a MacBook. Samsung and Huawei's designs include their respective logotypes, while the designs from Microsoft, WhatsApp, Telegram, and JoyPixels show their logomarks. The Twitter Emoji Stickers use the legacy Twitter bird, whereas Google’s design features a blob-style smiley face.

A woman behind a computer screen, working in the field of technology.

Usually shown working on a laptop, though Google's design previously appeared to be using a desktop computer instead.

The laptop in Apple's design includes the Apple logo, consistent with a MacBook. Samsung and Huawei's designs include their respective logotypes, while the designs from Microsoft, WhatsApp, Telegram, and JoyPixels show their logomarks. The Twitter Emoji Stickers use the legacy Twitter bird, whereas Google’s design features a blob-style smiley face.

A singer or rock star generally displayed with a microphone, and sometimes musical notes.

iOS and Android display this emoji as a Bowie-esque figure while WhatsApp appears heavily inspired by Prince.

A man singer or rock star generally displayed with a microphone, and sometimes musical notes.

iOS and Android display this emoji as a Bowie-esque figure while WhatsApp appears heavily inspired by Prince.

A woman singer or rock star generally displayed with a microphone, and sometimes musical notes.

iOS and Android display this emoji as a Bowie-esque figure while WhatsApp appears heavily inspired by Prince.
A person engaged in the visual art of painting, shown holding a palette and paintbrush.
A man engaged in the visual art of painting, shown holding a palette and paintbrush.
A woman engaged in the visual art of painting, shown holding a palette and paintbrush.
A person tasked with flying an aircraft, such as an ✈ Airplane or a 🚁 Helicopter, shown wearing a traditional airline pilot uniform.
A man tasked with flying an aircraft, such as an ✈ Airplane or a 🚁 Helicopter, shown wearing a traditional airline pilot uniform.
A woman tasked with flying an aircraft, such as an ✈ Airplane or a 🚁 Helicopter, shown wearing a traditional airline pilot uniform.
An astronaut or cosmonaut shown wearing a space suit and helmet.
A male astronaut or cosmonaut shown wearing a space suit and helmet.
A female astronaut or cosmonaut shown wearing a space suit and helmet.
A person professionally tasked with controlling and extinguishing fires.
A man professionally tasked with controlling and extinguishing fires.
A woman professionally tasked with controlling and extinguishing fires.

A police officer wearing a blue hat with a gold badge or shield in the middle.

See also 👮‍♀ Woman Police Officer or 👮‍♂ Man Police Officer
The male version of the 👮 Police Officer emoji. Currently identical in appearance to the non-gendered base emoji.
The female version of the 👮 Police Officer emoji.

An undercover investigator, wearing a hat and usually using a magnifying glass to search for clues or closely inspect evidence.

May be used to represent doing research or carrying out a personal investigation, like snooping around. Can also suggest that someone trying to be sneaky has been caught or noticed.

When emoji skin tone modifier sequences were first introduced, this emoji was not initially recommended to support them. However, a proposal was later submitted to address this, and it was subsequently adopted.
The male version of the 🕵 Sleuth or Spy emoji. Currently identical in appearance to the non-gendered base emoji.
The female version of the 🕵 Sleuth or Spy emoji.
A British guardsman, known as a foot guard. Wears a tall black hat with a yellow chin-strap. Must look straight ahead at all times, even when tourists attempt to distract them.
The male version of the 💂 Guardsman emoji. Currently identical in appearance to the non-gendered base emoji.
The female version of the 💂 Guardsman emoji.

A person dressed as a ninja with a black hood, a mask covering the lower half of their face, and the hilt of a knife or sword emerging from behind their shoulder.

This emoji is considered racist in some contexts, particularly when used to disparage, insult, and abuse people with dark skin, especially Black people.

The now-discontinued Microsoft ZWJ sequence 🐱‍👤 Ninja Cat did not include the ninja emoji at all as it was developed several years before ninja was approved. It combined 🐱 Cat Face and 👤 Bust in Silhouette and was only available from Microsoft prior to the debut of the Fluent emoji set in November 2021.

A construction worker wearing a hard-hat (safety helmet). Has a high visibility vest or hammer in some variations.

Some platforms display a green cross on the helmet which is used in Japan as a safety reminder in construction zones. It is also commonly seen on the Met helmet in the game Mega Man.
The male version of the 👷 Construction Worker emoji.
The female version of the 👷 Construction Worker emoji.
👸 Princess and 🤴 Prince were added in 2015 and 2016, respectively. Person With Crown was created to represent royalty without being overly specific about gender.

Male royalty, intended as a gender pair for the princess emoji. Shown as a man with a crown.

Not a reference to the musician Prince, however the man singer emoji on WhatsApp does show a character that bears a heavy resemblance to this artist.
The face of a princess; a girl or woman wearing a small crown or tiara. Could also be used to represent a Queen or other royalty.
A person dressed for a formal occasion, wearing a tuxedo. No gender is specified for this emoji. See also Woman in Tuxedo and Man in Tuxedo.
A man dressed for a formal occasion, wearing a tuxedo.
A woman dressed for a formal occasion, wearing a tuxedo.
A person in traditional western wedding dress with a veil over their head.
A man wearing a traditional Western wedding dress with a veil over their head.
A woman wearing a traditional western wedding dress with a veil over their head.

Santa Claus, sometimes referred to as Father Christmas, brings joy to children at Christmas time. Displayed with a beard and red festive hat.

The Santa emoji had a frown on Android 4.4, which was resolved in Android 5.0. See also: Christmas emoji list.

Note: Father Christmas has a different origin to Santa Claus but both are represented by this single emoji.
Mother Christmas, more commonly known as Mrs. Claus, is the wife of Santa Claus. Displayed as an older woman with glasses and a festive red and white bonnet. See also: Christmas emoji list.

A person, generally depicted as being older with gray hair, wearing a red Christmas (aka "Santa") hat. Does not represent any specific character in folklore. Mx Claus provides a gender inclusive alternative to 🎅 Santa Claus or 🤶 Mrs. Claus.

Apple depicts Mx Claus as wearing glasses, while other vendors do not.

Mx is an honorific that does not indicate gender.

A person who wields abilities beyond those of ordinary people and is dedicated to protecting the public. Generally depicted as wearing a colorful domino mask and a cape.

This base emoji does not specify a gender, but is used to create the emojis for Man Superhero and Woman Superhero.

The Supervillain is the nemesis of this emoji.

A man who wields abilities beyond those of ordinary people and is dedicated to protecting the public. Generally depicted as wearing a colorful domino mask and a cape.

The Supervillain is the nemesis of this emoji.

A woman who wields abilities beyond those of ordinary people and is dedicated to protecting the public. Generally depicted as wearing a colorful domino mask and a cape.

The Supervillain is the nemesis of this emoji.

A person who wields abilities beyond those of ordinary people who, unlike their nemesis the Superhero, uses their powers for evil.

This base emoji does not specify a gender, but is used to create the emojis for Man Supervillain and Woman Supervillain.

Google's design is similar to that of Mr. Sinister from the X-Men Marvel comics.

A man who wields abilities beyond those of ordinary people who, unlike their nemesis the Superhero, uses their powers for evil.

Google's design is similar to that of Mr. Sinister from the X-Men Marvel comics.

A woman who wields abilities beyond those of ordinary people who, unlike their nemesis the Superhero, uses their powers for evil.

Google's design is similar to that of Mr. Sinister from the X-Men Marvel comics.
A person who wields magical powers derived from supernatural or occult sources.

A man who wields magical powers derived from supernatural or occult sources.

May also be referred to as a wizard, warlock, or sorcerer.
A woman who wields magical powers derived from supernatural or occult sources. May also be referred to as a witch, enchantress, or sorceress.

A magical humanoid creature found in myths and fantasy stories. Generally depicted as having insect-inspired wings, it can also be assumed to be quite diminutive in size.

This emoji supports skin tones, and variations that are female or male.
A magical male creature found in myths and fantasy stories. Generally depicted as having insect-inspired wings, it can also be assumed to be quite diminutive in size.
A magical female creature found in myths and fantasy stories. Generally depicted as having insect-inspired wings, it can also be assumed to be quite diminutive in size.

A vampire shown wearing a dark cape, and with pointed fangs. This emoji supports skin tones, and variations that are female or male.

May be used to call someone an "energy vampire", i.e. a person whose actions leave others exhausted or drained of energy
A male vampire shown wearing a dark cape, and with pointed fangs.
A female vampire shown wearing a dark cape, and with pointed fangs.

A merperson who may be referred to as merfolk or merpeople in plural. May be used for the display of a mermaid, mergirl, merwoman, or merman.

Occasional shown wielding a trident.
The male version of the 🧜 Merperson emoji.
The female version of the 🧜 Merperson emoji.

A mythical creature with pointed ears and a human-like face, originating in folklore.

While depictions of elves vary across cultures and traditions, this emoji's design is heavily influenced by the portrayal of elves popularized in modern high fantasy literature, particularly The Lord of the Rings. As such, most vendors display the creature wearing elegant robes and often wearing an ornate headpiece.

Even still, this emoji may be used to discuss Santa's helpers, especially around Christmas.
A male creature with pointed ears and a human-like face.
A female creature with pointed ears and a human-like face.

A supernatural being, which is generally shown to be imprisoned within a bottle or lamp. May be capable of granting wishes when summoned. Variations exist for a female genie or male genie.

Several vendors' design for this emoji is highly reminiscent of The Genie character from Disney's Aladdin films.
A supernatural male being, which is generally shown to be imprisoned within a bottle or lamp. May be capable of granting wishes when summoned.
A supernatural female being, which is generally shown to be imprisoned within a bottle or lamp. May be capable of granting wishes when summoned.

A reanimated human, often found in works of horror fiction. May have a female or male appearance.

May be used to refer to someone who appears listless, apathetic, or unresponsive to their surroundings.

May also be used to refer to a person who attempts to resume communications after previously ghosting out of a conversation.
A reanimated human man, often found in works of horror fiction.
A reanimated human woman, often found in works of horror fiction.

A green troll, usually shown holding a club.

May be used to refer to the fantasy creature. May also be used to refer to an internet troll or the act of trolling.

Apple’s troll holds a scepter instead of a club. Microsoft, Twitter, and WhatsApp's designs show only the bust of a troll instead of the full-bodied creature.

A large hairy humanoid cryptid, inspired by various global myths and legends.

Google's design mimics the posture of the famous still from the 1967 'Bigfoot' sighting footage.

Two people holding hands, most likely due to being in a relationship.

No gender is specified for these two people, meaning they are likely to be shown with a gender inclusive design.
Two women holding hands, most likely due to being in a relationship.
A woman and man holding hands, most likely due to being in a relationship.
Two men holding hands, most likely due to being in a relationship.

A kissing gesture, shown with a pink love heart floating in the air between two people. No gender is specified for the two people, and as such this may be used to represent the concept of a couple broadly, and/or as a means of showing two non-binary people.

Previously shown with the same appearance as 👩‍❤‍💋‍👨 Kiss: Woman, Man, but now displays two people with an ambiguous gender appearance.
A woman and a man displayed kissing, or gesturing a kiss toward each other.
Two men displayed kissing, or gesturing a kiss toward each other. At small sizes this may be difficult to discern from the two women kissing.
Two women displayed kissing, or gesturing a kiss toward each other. At small sizes this may be difficult to discern from two men kissing.

A couple standing next to each other, smiling, with a love heart floating in the air between them. No gender is specified for the two people, and as such this may be used to represent the concept of a couple broadly, and/or as a means of showing two non-binary people.

Previously shown with the same appearance as 👩‍❤‍👨 Couple With Heart: Woman, Man, but now displays two people with an ambiguous gender appearance.
A woman and a man standing next to each other, smiling, with a love heart floating in the air between them.
Two men standing next to each other, smiling, with a love heart floating in the air between them.

A family unit shown with two adults and one child. Previously displayed with the same design as 👨‍👩‍👦 Family: Man, Woman, Boy on most platforms, but now has its own gender inclusive appearance.

A family unit shown with two adults and one child.

Usually depicted as a collection of silhouettes on a block color background, as per Unicode's recommendations.

A family unit shown with two adults and two children.

Usually depicted as a collection of silhouettes on a block color background, as per Unicode's recommendations.

A family unit shown with one adult and one child.

Usually depicted as a collection of silhouettes on a block color background, as per Unicode's recommendations.

A family unit shown with one adult and two children.

Usually depicted as a collection of silhouettes on a block color background, as per Unicode's recommendations.

A friendly, cartoon-styled face of a monkey, looking straight ahead. Depicted as a brown-haired monkey with a tan or pinkish face, round ears, nostrils, and open-mouthed grin.

As with the full-bodied 🐒 Monkey, often used with a playful tone or for metaphorical senses of monkey.

One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac. Available as an Apple Animoji.

Vendors implement the same or similar monkey face in their Three Wise Monkeys emojis: 🙈 See-No-Evil Monkey, 🙉 Hear-No-Evil Monkey, and 🙊 Speak-No-Evil Monkey.

Facebook’s monkey previously resembled 🐻 Bear Face.

This emoji is considered racist in some contexts, particularly when used to disparage, insult, and abuse people with dark skin, especially Black people.

A monkey, a small primate with long limbs and tail for climbing trees. Generally depicted as a cartoon-styled, brown monkey with a cheeky facial expression, shown in full profile facing left, sitting on its hind legs with a long, curled tail and round ears.

As with 🐵 Monkey Face, often used with a playful tone or for metaphorical senses of monkey.

One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac.

WhatsApp’s monkey is facing right, Facebook’s has shaggy hair.

This emoji is considered racist in some contexts, particularly when used to disparage, insult, and abuse people with dark skin, especially Black people.

A gorilla, the powerful, black-haired great ape. Variously depicted in full profile on all fours facing left or as a friendly, cartoon-styled gorilla face looking straight ahead.

Most platforms' designs depict a full gorilla, as a silverback, with strong shoulders and reddish forehead.

Twitter’s designs previously featured a black and gray gorilla face with a neutral expression and prominent forehead and jaw. Google, Samsung, and Facebook’s designs also previously featured only a gorilla face.

This emoji is considered racist in some contexts, particularly when used to disparage, insult, and abuse people with dark skin, especially Black people.

An orangutan, the orange-haired ape with long arms. Depicted facing forward, with a long broad face and sitting with its legs bent. Occasionally shown scratching its head. Color varies across platforms, ranging from orange to light brown.

This emoji is considered racist in some contexts, particularly when used to disparage, insult, and abuse people with dark skin, especially Black people.

A friendly, cartoon-styled face of a dog, looking straight ahead. Depicted as the face of a dog of various breeds, generally light-brown and white, with pointed or floppy ears and its tongue hanging out.

May be used with a more playful tone than the full-bodied 🐕 Dog, though their applications generally overlap. See also 🐩 Poodle.

One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac. Available as an Apple Animoji.

Many vendors implement the same or similar dog as their full-bodied 🐕 Dog, such as Google and Facebook. Apple and WhatsApp’s dogs have a white face with brown, floppy ears and a brown patch over one eye.

Included in the earliest Japanese emoji sets from Softbank, Docomo, and au by KDDI.

A dog, a faithful, beloved pet canine. Depicted as a light-brown dog, of various breeds, in full profile on all fours facing left, with a long, curled tail held upright and pointed or floppy ears.

Apple and Facebook’s dogs resemble a reddish-brown Shiba Inu, a popular Japanese breed featured in the Doge meme. Google shows what appears to be a Beagle.

See also 🐩 Poodle and 🐶 Dog Face, whose applications may overlap. Some vendors implement the same or a similar dog in their 🦮 Guide Dog and 🐕‍🦺 Service Dog.

One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac.

Google and Facebook previously featured puppies with collars, Apple’s dog previously resembled an Akita Inu, another popular Japanese breed.

A guide (or Seeing Eye) dog, trained to help lead a person who is blind or visually impaired. Generally depicted as a yellowish-brown Labrador Retriever on all fours facing left, equipped with a harness and handle. Many platforms additionally include a collar.

Not to be confused with 🐕‍🦺 Service Dog, though their popular applications may overlap.

Twitter implements the same dog as its 🐕 Dog. Samsung and Twitter’s guide dogs have green harnesses.

A service animal displayed with a safety vest and lead. Differs from the guide dog as this animal is intended for detection of seizures or other “hidden disabilities”, according to the proposal from Apple.

A poodle, a popular dog breed with curly hair, often groomed in an ornamental pattern.

Generally depicted as a grayish-white poodle in full profile on all fours facing left, with a shaved torso, legs, and face with fuller, pom-pom-like hair on its head, ears, chest, feet, and tip of tail (as the Continental Clip).

Like 🐕 Dog, may be used to represent a variety of dog breeds (often fluffy or long-haired). See also 🐶 Dog Face.

Google, Samsung, and Facebook’s designs previously featured pink poodles.

The face of a wolf, a howling canine that hunts in packs. Generally depicted as a cartoon-styled face of a gray wolf with pointed ears, white cheeks and muzzle, and black nose.

Its expression is variously neutral, friendly, or slightly menacing, as in Google and Samsung’s designs. Apple and Huawei's designs features the head of gray wolf, facing left.

Occasionally used to represent metaphorical senses of wolf, e.g., lone wolf, wolf pack.

Apple and SoftBank’s designs previously resembled a reddish-brown canine, resembling a dog or fox.

A friendly, cartoon-styled faced of a fox, the cunning canine, looking straight ahead. Depicted as an orange fox  face with a black nose, pointed ears, and shaggy, white cheeks.

Often used with an affectionate or playful tone (e.g., slang, foxy). Does not have a full-bodied fox emoji counterpart.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

A raccoon, a nocturnal mammal with a mask around its eyes. Generally depicted as a friendly, cartoon-styled, gray raccoon face looking straight ahead, with black-and-white markings around its eyes and pointed ears and cheeks.

Apple and WhatsApp’s designs feature a raccoon in full profile on all fours facing left with a striped, bushy tail.

Meow! A friendly, cartoon-styled face of a cat, looking straight ahead. Generally depicted as a yellowish-orange cat face with pointed ears and whiskers.

May be used with a more affectionate tone than the full-bodied 🐈 Cat, though their applications generally overlap.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

Vendors implement the same or similar cat in their 🐈 Cat as well as in their cat-faced variants of smileys:

Google’s cat face was previously orange, Samsung’s gray, and Facebook’s once gray and white. Included in the earliest Japanese emoji sets from Softbank, Docomo, and au by KDDI.

A domestic cat, beloved as a pet. Generally depicted as a light-orange cat with stripes, as a tabby, in full profile on all fours facing left, with its long tell held upright.

Google’s cat is cartoon-styled, shown sitting on its hind legs with a friendly expression and whiskers. Facebook’s cat is a gray tabby, though previously was orange. Microsoft and Samsung’s cats were previously gray, Twitter’s brown.
A black cat shown in full profile, often with its tail curling upward.

A friendly, cartoon-styled face of a lion—the large cat and king of the jungle—looking straight ahead.

Depicted as a golden-yellow lion face with a light- or dark-brown mane, white muzzle, and neutral expression. Does not have a full-bodied lion emoji counterpart.

A lion is represented as ♌ Leo in the Western zodiac.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

Apple's lion previously featured a timid-looking expression.

A friendly, cartoon-styled face of a tiger looking straight ahead. Generally depicted in yellowish-orange with black stripes on its forehead and cheeks, a white muzzle, and neutral expression.

Often used with a more affectionate tone than the full-bodied 🐅 Tiger.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

A tiger, a large cat with an orange coat and black stripes. Depicted in full profile on all fours facing left, with a long tail, its distinctive stripes, and, on some platforms, white patches.

See also 🐯 Tiger Face. Not to be confused with 🐆 Leopard.

One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac.

Frequently associated with the Cincinnati Bengals, an American football team.

Google’s design is noticeably more cartoon-styled, as Facebook’s previously was. Microsoft’s design previously featured a yellow, forward-facing tiger, as if on the prowl.

A leopard, a large cat with a yellowish-brown coat and black-and-gold spots. Depicted in full profile on all fours facing left, with a long tail and its distinctive pattern.

Sometimes used to represent jaguars, panthers, cheetahs, and related cats. May also be used to indicate leopard prints in fashion. Not to be confused with 🐅 Tiger.

Frequently associated with the Jacksonville Jaguars, an American football team.

Google’s design is noticeably more cartoon-styled. Microsoft’s design was previously solid yellowish-brown in color, resembling a cougar or mountain lion.

The face of a horse, generally facing left. Depicted as a light or reddish-brown horse with a dark brown or black mane, and, on many platforms, a light-colored muzzle.

Not to be confused with the full-bodied 🐎 Horse or 🏇 Horse Racing, though their applications may overlap. Some vendors implement a similar design in 🦄 Unicorn Face and 🦓 Zebra.

WhatsApp’s horse is facing left, as Facebook’s previously was. Microsoft’s horse was previously looking straight ahead, as was Samsung’s, shown with a goofy, full-toothed grin. Softbank previously featured a full-bodied horse.

A moose head with large antlers.

Can be used to talk about the actual animal. Can also be used to represent countries, including Canada and Sweden, where the moose is considered a national symbol. Can also be used alongside the phrase "cool as a moose."

Google’s Moose is facing left, while Twitter displays a full-bodied moose.

A grey donkey or mule, shown in full profile, sometimes with its hind legs kicking into the air.

Can be used literally to represent the pack animal. Can also be used metaphorically to call someone a jackass or to say that someone is stubborn as a mule.

Because the donkey is a symbol of the Democratic Party of the United States, it may be used in political contexts. Additionally, the term mule can refer to someone who carries illegal drugs across borders, so this emoji may be used to talk about smugglers and the act of smuggling.

A horse, a hoofed mammal used for riding and racing. Depicted as a brown horse in full profile galloping to the left, with a dark, flowing mane and tail.

May be used to represent various types of horses and their metaphorical senses (e.g., mustang, stallion).

May also be used as a compliment to an attractive person.

One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac.a

Not to be confused with 🐴 Horse Face, 🎠 Carousel Horse, and 🏇 Horse Racing, which features a jockey on its back.

Apple’s horse is wearing a green saddle blanket, Facebook’s a blue blanket with saddle. SoftBank’s design previously featured a racing horse with a jockey.

The face of a unicorn, a mythical creature in the form of a white horse with a single, long horn on its forehead. Generally depicted as a white horse head facing left with a pink or purple mane and a yellow or rainbow-colored horn.

In addition to the mythical unicorn, may be used to convey whimsy, fantasy, uniqueness, specialness, peace, and love. Often used for various content related to the LGBTQ community, thanks in part to its rainbow colors on many platforms. Also often used in association with “unicorn” startups. Sometimes used as a rainbow or holographic accent color.

Vendors implement the emoji with the same or similar design as 🐴 Horse Face, but with colorful hair and a horn.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

WhatsApp’s unicorn is facing right. Google’s unicorn previously had a brown mane, Samsung’s a pink mane. Twitter’s unicorn was previously purple-colored with a blue mane.

A zebra, a horse-like mammal with black-and-white stripes. Variously depicted in full profile on all fours facing left or, less commonly, as a zebra head facing left with a short mane.

Occasionally used in a humorous way to refer to “prison stripes,” due to the resemblance between zebra markings and classic black-and-white inmate uniforms.

Not to be confused with 🐎 Horse. Some vendors implement a similar face as their 🐴 Horse Face.

Apple, Microsoft, WhatsApp, Samsung, and Facebook’s designs feature the full animal; Google and Twitter's designs feature a head with a short mane and black muzzle. Facebook’s design previously featured only a zebra head, as did Samsung's.

A deer, a fleet-footed, hoofed mammal whose males (bucks, stags) generally have antlers. Variously depicted as a light-brown deer in full profile on all fours facing left or as a deer face looking straight head; both depictions feature large, branched antlers.

May be used to represent elk, moose, antelope, or reindeer, especially in connection with Christmas. Most platforms display a deer in full profile. Twitter shows a deer face.

Google’s deer previously had a red nose, as Rudolph the Red-nosed Reindeer. Apple and WhatsApp’s deers are white-tailed.

A brown bison shown in full profile with horns, a beard, and woolly mane. Also called a buffalo in North America.

This emoji is frequently associated with the Buffalo Bills, an American football team.

A friendly, cartoon-styled face of a cow looking straight ahead. Variously depicted as a white, brown, or multicolored cow face with a neutral expression, short horns, and a pink or brown muzzle.

Often used with a more affectionate tone than the full-bodied 🐄 Cow.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

Facebook’s design once featured a more lifelike, brown cow face.

An ox, a bovine used as a draft animal. Depicted in brown in full profile on all fours facing left, with a tail and short horns.

One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac. Often used to represent ♉ Taurus (the Bull) in the Western zodiac. 2021 is Year of the Ox.

Often used to represent a bull and occasionally paired with 💩 Pile of Poo to stand in for slang terms. Not to be confused with 🐃 Water Buffalo.

A water buffalo, a bovine used to plough rice fields in parts of Asia. Depicted in gray or black in full profile on all fours facing left, with a tail and broad horns curled up at the tips.

Often used to represent a bull. Not to be confused with 🐂 Ox, though their applications may overlap.

Microsoft’s design was previously brown.

A cow, a bovine farmed for its meat or milk. Depicted in full profile on all fours facing left with a black-and-white patched coat (as a Holstein Friesian) and, on many platforms, a pink udder and horns.

May be used to represent the animal, its food products, or black-and-white coloring. See also 🐮 Cow Face.

Microsoft's cow was previously brown, as was Facebook's, which had a bell around its neck.

A friendly, cartoon-styled face of a pig looking straight ahead. Depicted as a pink face with a neutral expression, pointed or floppy ears, and a distinctive pig nose.

Often used with a more affectionate tone than the full-bodied 🐖 Pig. However, it can also be used metaphorically to describe someone as gluttonous or messy.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

Apple’s face bears a slight grin and previously featured floppy ears.

A pig, a plump animal farmed for its meat, such as bacon. Depicted in light pink in full profile on all fours facing left, with a long snout and short, curly tail.

May be used to represent the animal, its food products, or various metaphorical senses of pig. As such, it can be used to describe someone as gluttonous or messy.

One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac; 2019 is the Year of the Pig. See also 🐷 Pig Face, 🐽 Pig Nose, and 🐗 Boar.

WhatsApp’s design previously featured a wide grin.

A boar, a hairy, wild pig with tusks. Generally depicted as the face of a brown boar, either facing left or looking straight ahead, with prominent tusks projecting from its lower jaw.

Twitter's design feature a friendly, cartoon-styled face, as did an early Facebook design. WhatsApp’s design displays the animal in full, as Google, Microsoft, and Samsung previously did.

Not to be confused with 🐖 Pig or 🐷 Pig Face, though their applications may overlap.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

The snout of a pig. Depicted as a pink oval or slightly pear-shaped nose with two black nostrils.

Like 🐖 Pig and 🐷 Pig Face, it may be used metaphorically to describe someone as gluttonous or messy.

Previously displayed as a cute pig character on Google Gmail.

A ram, a male sheep with large, spiraling horns. Generally depicted in full profile on all fours facing left with a thick, white fleece and light-brown horns.

Occasionally used to represent antelopes and related animals. Not to be confused with 🐑 Ewe, though their applications may overlap.

Often considered (in lieu of 🐐 Goat) one of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac. Also often used to represent ♈ Aries (the Ram) in the Western zodiac.

WhatsApp and Facebook’s designs resemble a bighorn sheep, as Apple’s once did. Google's design previously had its eyes closed.

A ewe, or female sheep raised for its wool, meat, and milk. Depicted in full profile on all fours facing left with a thick, white fleece and black, gray, or white skin, and lacking the large, spiraling horns seen on a ram.

As such, this emoji is not to be confused with the 🐏 Ram emoji, though their applications may overlap. Additionally often considered one of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac in lieu of the 🐐 Goat.

In 2025, this emoji became the most-used emoji on the social platform Bluesky, driven by the account counting sheep, which posted threads featuring an ever-increasing number of this emoji every 15 minutes.

Apple and Google’s designs previously depicted a ram. Samsung and Facebook’s designs previously featured only a ewe face.

A goat, a sturdy, hoofed animal raised for its meat and milk. Depicted as a light brown, white, or multicored goat in full profile on all fours facing left, a scraggly beard, upright tail, and brown or yellow horns curving back.

Frequently used as a visual shorthand for the slang expression GOAT, or the Great of All Time, often said of athletes and in particular the late Kobe Bryant.

Often considered one of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac. Also often used to represent ♑ Capricorn in the Western zodiac.

Apple, Google, and Samsung’s goats were previously white, as a Saanen goat. Facebook’s design previously featured only a goat face.

A dromedary camel, a long-necked mammal with one large hump on its back. Depicted in light or yellowish brown in full profile on all fours facing left.

Not to be confused with 🐫 Two-Hump Camel (Bactrian), though their applications generally overlap.

May be used in association with deserts, the Middle East, and Wednesday (Hump Day).

Samsung’s design features a camel with a shaggy head of hair and slight smile. Google’s design previously featured a blanket on its back, as for transport.

A Bactrian camel, a long-necked mammal with two large humps on its back. Depicted in light or yellowish brown, sometimes with a shaggy mane and humps, in full profile on all fours facing left.

Not to be confused with 🐪 Camel (dromedary), though their applications generally overlap.

May be used in association with deserts, the Middle East and Central Asia, and Wednesday (Hump Day).

Samsung’s design features a camel with a shaggy head of hair and slight smile. Google’s design previously featured a blanket on its back, as for transport.

A llama, a long-necked, camel-like animal, native to South America and used for transport and wool. Depicted as a shaggy white, light-brown, or multicolored llama in full profile on all fours facing left.

May be used to represent an alpaca or related animals.

A giraffe, the tallest animal on Earth, with spots and a long neck. Generally depicted in yellow or tan in full profile on all fours facing left, with distinctive brown spots and small, horn-like structures.

Samsung’s designs feature a giraffe face looking straight ahead. Facebook’s design previously featured only a giraffe face, as did Microsoft's.
A brown wooly mammoth with large curved tusks. Can also be used to represent a mastodon.

A rhinoceros, a large mammal with one or two massive horns on its nose. Generally shown in light gray with two horns, depicted in full profile on all fours or as a rhinoceros head looking left.

Resembles the white or black rhinoceros.

Apple, Google, Microsoft, WhatsApp, and Facebook’s designs feature the full animal, while Samsung and Twitter’s designs feature only the rhinoceros' head.

Facebook’s design previously featured just the rhinoceros' head, as did Google's.

A friendly, cartoon-styled face of a mouse, looking straight ahead. Generally depicted as a gray or white mouse face with large, round ears, a pink, pointed nose, and whiskers.

Often used with a more affectionate tone than the full-bodied 🐁 Mouse. Not to be confused with 🐹 Hamster Face.

Google and Facebook’s designs feature a mouse with buck teeth. Microsoft’s design was previously brown.

Eek! A mouse, a small rodent with large ears and a long tail. Generally depicted in white in full profile on all fours facing left, with pink ears, feet, and tail, often with reddish eyes.

See also 🐭 Mouse Face. Not to be confused with 🐀 Rat or 🖱 Computer Mouse.

Facebook’s mouse is sitting on its hind legs. Google’s design was previously more cartoon-styled, standing on its hind legs and facing forward with a buck tooth. Microsoft’s mouse was previously brown.

A rat, a large rodent with a long tail, known to frequent big cities. Depicted in gray in full profile on all fours facing left, with pink ears, feet, and tail.

May be use for various metaphorical senses of rat, including as an insult. Not to be confused with 🐁 Mouse, which has white hair.

One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac.

Google’s design was previously standing on its hind legs and facing forward with a buck tooth.

A friendly, cartoon-styled face of a hamster—a small rodent often kept as a pet—looking straight ahead. Generally depicted as a brown-and-white faced hamster with whiskers, a pink nose, puffy cheeks, and large, round, pink ears, sometimes with a buck tooth.

Often used with an affectionate tone. May be used to represent a gerbil, guinea pig, chinchilla, or related animals. Does not have a full-bodied hamster emoji counterpart.

Not to be confused with 🐭 Mouse Face.

Microsoft’s hamster was previously gray.

A friendly, cartoon-styled face of a rabbit, looking straight ahead. Generally depicted as a gray and/or white rabbit face with upright ears and pink ears and nose, often with whiskers and a buck tooth.

Often used with a more affectionate tone than the full-bodied 🐇 rabbit. Also often used to represent the Easter Bunny.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

Microsoft’s rabbit face was previously pink-colored with one ear flopping down. Facebook’s rabbit face was previously gray-colored with both ears flopping down.

A rabbit, a hoppy mammal with long ears. Depicted as a white, gray, or brown rabbit in full profile facing left with pink ears and a short tail, sitting on its long, hind legs or on all fours.

May be used in association with spring, Easter, magic, bunny ears, or various rabbit-based characters or expressions (e.g., going down the rabbit hole).

See also 🐰 Rabbit Face. One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac.

Apple’s rabbit has red eyes, WhatsApp’s whiskers. Microsoft’s rabbit was previously brown, Facebook’s white.

A chipmunk, a small rodent with puffy cheeks. Depicted as a brown chipmunk in full profile facing left, sitting on its hind legs with a bushy tail and striped body. Generally holding an acorn or other nut in its hands.

May be used to represent a squirrel or related animals.

At one point, Google’s chipmunk was looking forward, squinting with a buck tooth. Microsoft’s previous black-and-white design could be mistaken for a skunk.

A brown beaver with buckteeth and a wide paddle-like tail. Can be used in the context of actual beavers, or metaphorically to evoke qualities of beavers like working hard, as in the expression beavering away.

Commonly associated with Canada, as beavers are a national emblem of the country. May also be used in reference to the vagina, which is an informal sense of the word beaver.

A hedgehog. A small, spiny mammal sometimes kept as a pet. Generally depicted in full profile on all fours facing left, with a round, brown body covered with spines and a light-brown face and underside.

Sometimes used to represent a porcupine or echidna.

Twitter's design has always been a hedgehog facing forward. Google's design originally featured a hedgehog facing forward, though it was changed to full profile with Android 11.0. Facebook’s design previously featured a hedgehog on its back, rolled up in a ball.

A bat, the flying mammal of the night. Variously depicted as a brown, black, or gray bat, with wings outspread and pointy ears, facing forward or left.

Often used in association with Halloween, vampires, and Batman.

Google’s bat was previously purplish in color, bearing two fangs. Samsung’s bat was previously brown, and Facebook’s gray.

A friendly, cartoon-styled face of bear, looking straight ahead. Depicted as a brown bear with round ears and a tan muzzle. Resembles a teddy bear.

Often used with an affectionate tone. Does not have a full-bodied bear emoji counterpart.

May be used to refer to certain members of the LGBTQ community, a la the slang term "bear".

Available as an Apple Animoji.

Samsung’s bear was previously golden brown.

A friendly, cartoon-styled face of polar bear, looking straight ahead. Depicted as the face of a white bear with round ears.

WhatsApp previously showed the full body of the bear.

A friendly, cartoon-styled face of a koala—a bear-like marsupial known for eating eucalyptus and sleeping—looking straight ahead. Depicted as a gray face with round, fluffy ears and a large, black nose.

Often used with an affectionate tone and in association with Australia, where the animal is found.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

Google previously depicted a full-bodied koala climbing a tree, Softbank’s koala previously had brown fur.

A friendly, cartoon-styled face of a panda—a bear-like mammal known for eating bamboo—looking straight ahead. Depicted as a white panda face with black ears and black circles around its eyes.

Often used with an affectionate tone and in association with China, where the animal is found. Sometimes used to represent a red panda. Does not have a full-bodied panda emoji counterpart.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

Google and Facebook’s pandas are shown smiling with an open mouth and tongue.

A sloth, the slow-moving, tree-dwelling mammal. Depicted as a light-brown sloth with a wide, whitish, masked face hanging from a tree branch, facing left or right. Generally shown as a three-toed sloth.

An otter, the playful water mammal in the weasel family. Depicted as a light-brown otter on its back, with its forepaws held together and whiskered face to the left, generally with its long tail curled up.

May be used to refer to certain members of the LGBTQ community, a la the slang term "otter".

Apple’s otter is in water, holding a stone, as is Microsoft’s.

A skunk, a bushy-tailed mammal that sprays a foul odor when threatened. Depicted in full profile on all fours facing left, with black hair and its distinctive white stripe running from its head down to a curled-up tail.

Google’s original skunk design bore a humorously haughty air.

A kangaroo, a marsupial with a large tail and legs. Depicted in yellowish-brown in full profile facing left with large, pointed ears, shown either resting on its hind legs and tail or jumping.

Commonly used in connection with Australia, where the animal is found.

OpenMoji initially displayed a 🦩 Flamingo design for this emoji in error.

A badger, a stocky mammal in the weasel family with a long, pointed head. Generally depicted in full profile on all fours facing left, with a gray coat, black-and-white-striped face, and short tail.

Google’s design used to feature a friendly, cartoon-styled black-and-white badger face. Facebook’s badger is sitting on its hind legs.

A pair of paw prints, as left by a pet 🐈 cat or 🐕 dog. Generally depicted as two, staggered, dark-colored paw prints, each showing four toes and a pad.

Commonly used for various content concerning pet cats and dogs. Occasionally applied to other quadruped mammals. See also 👣 Footprints.

Apple, Google and Facebook’s prints were previously red, while Microsoft’s were orange. Facebook's earliest design originally displayed human footprints.

A turkey, a gobbling bird traditionally eaten at Thanksgiving or Christmas. Depicted in full profile facing left, standing on its legs with a dark-brown body, a white-fringed plume, pink or blue head, and its distinctive red snood and wattle.

May be consumed in the form of 🍗 Poultry Leg.

A chicken, a bird used for its meat and eggs. Generally depicted as the white head of a chicken (hen or rooster) looking left, with a yellow beak, red comb on its head, and red wattle on its neck.

May be consumed in the form of 🍗 Poultry Leg. Not to be confused with the full-bodied 🐓 Rooster, though their applications overlap. Also may be used for metaphorical senses of chicken (e.g., “coward”).

See also 🐣 Hatching Chick, 🐤 Baby Chick, and 🐥 Front-Facing Baby Chick.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

Twitter’s chicken head is looking straight ahead. Microsoft’s chicken was previously yellow, while Samsung’s faced forward; Facebook’s design once featured a full, brown bird, while Google’s design previously featured a full bodied chicken.

A rooster (cock), a male chicken known for its cock-a-doodle-do. Depicted as a white or multicolored rooster standing on its legs in full profile facing left, with a red comb on its head and red wattle on its neck.

Not to be confused with 🐔 Chicken, though their applications overlap. See also 🐣 Hatching Chick, 🐤 Baby Chick, and 🐥 Front-Facing Baby Chick. Occasionally used as sexual slang.

One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac.

Google’s rooster is brown with a green tail, Facebook’s brown with a blue tail. Google’s rooster was previously white, Microsoft’s yellow, Samsung’s looking straight ahead.

A baby chicken (chick), hatching from an egg and seeing the world for the first time. Depicted as a yellow chick with an orange beak facing forward in the cracked, bottom half of a white egg, generally shown flapping its wings with a cute facial expression.

Often used with an affectionate tone. May be used to represent various types of baby birds. May also be used to represent chicken foods (e.g., poultry, eggs), spring, Easter, or slang senses of chick.

Not to be confused with 🐤 Baby Chick or 🐥Front-Facing Baby Chick (out of its egg), though their applications overlap. See also 🐔 Chicken and 🐓 Rooster.

Twitter and Facebook's designs do not include wings. Google's design previously featured motion lines around the chick's wings, indicating flapping. Facebook's design previously showed part of the egg atop the chick's head.

A yellow baby chicken (chick). Variously depicted as a chick in full profile, standing on its legs, or as a chick head. Both designs show the bird facing left, with an orange beak and feet.

Often used with an affectionate tone. May be used to represent various types of baby birds. May also be used to represent chicken foods (e.g., poultry, eggs), spring, Easter, or slang senses of chick.

Not to be confused with 🐣 Hatching Chick or 🐥Front-Facing Baby Chick, though their applications overlap. See also 🐔 Chicken and 🐓 Rooster.

Apple, WhatsApp, and Facebook’s designs feature a chick head; other major platforms display a full-bodied chick.

A baby chicken (chick), shown as if flapping its wings. Depicted as a yellow chick with an orange beak in full profile standing on its legs, generally with its wings raised.

Often used with an affectionate tone. May be used to represent various types of baby birds. May also be used to represent chicken foods (e.g., poultry, eggs), spring, Easter, or slang senses of chick.

Not to be confused with 🐤 Baby Chick or 🐣 Hatching Chick (still in its egg), though their applications overlap. See also 🐔 Chicken and 🐓 Rooster.

Facebook's design previously featured only a chick head facing forward.

A generic bird. Variously depicted as a blue or red bird, as a bluebird or cardinal, shown standing in full profile, or as a bird head. Both designs show the bird facing left.

May be used for a variety of wild and pet birds as well as for metaphorical senses of bird (e.g., birdie in golf).

Apple and WhatsApp’s designs feature a grayish bird head. Notably, WhatsApp’s version appears in the popular “Snake With a Party Hat” meme image.

Google, Samsung, and Facebook’s designs suggest a bluebird, Microsoft and Twitter’s a cardinal. Google’s bird previously resembled a canary, Samsung’s was previously green, and Microsoft and Twitter’s birds were once blue.

A penguin, a flightless bird adapted to water and ice. Variously depicted as a full, black-bodied penguin with a white belly and orange bill or as a penguin head.

Often used with an affectionate or playful tone or in association with the cold. Occasionally used to represent a puffin.

Apple and WhatsApp’s designs feature a penguin head, with Apple’s bearing a yellow patch on its head, as an emperor penguin. Other major platforms feature a penguin standing in full profile, facing forward or left.

A dove carrying an olive branch, a symbol of peace in Western and Judeo-Christian culture. Depicted as a white bird in full profile facing left, flying as it holds a green sprig in its beak.

Commonly used to represent such sentiments as peace, love, hope, and reconciliation. Can also be used to discuss someone after they have passed away, i.e. expressing hope that they are now "at peace".

Microsoft’s dove was previously flying right, without an olive branch.

A bald eagle, the majestic bird of prey with brown feathers and distinctive white head. Generally depicted facing left, with its wings outspread and talons out, as if swooping down to seize prey.

Commonly associated with the United States, whose national emblem is the bald eagle. May be used for other eagles and birds of prey (e.g., hawks). It is also often associated with the Philadelphia Eagles NFL team.

Google’s eagle used to have its wings tucked in, as if perched on a branch. Twitter’s design shows only the bust of an eagle. Apple’s 📰 Newspaper features its eagle on its masthead.

Quack! A duck, a waterbird with webbed feet. Depicted as a male (drake) mallard in full profile facing left, standing on its legs with gray and brown feathers, a yellow bill, and its distinctive green head.

May be consumed in the form of a 🍗 Poultry Leg. Occasionally used as a substitute for the F-word, due to rhyming and Apple's iPhone autocorrect.

Samsung’s design previously featured a yellow rubber ducky.
A speaker cone displayed without any sound waves.

A computer printer, as at a home office. Generally depicted as a grayish device with a power button and paper loaded in its tray, sometimes printing out a document. May be used for various content concerning printing, including as a Print icon, as well as for office work and technology more generally.

Not to be confused with 📠 Fax Machine.

A silver optical disc, as a CD or DVD, used to play music or movies before the rise of streaming technology. Commonly used to represent CDs, DVDs, Blu-rays, and related film and music content, especially albums.

See also 💽 Computer Disk and 📀 DVD.

A place to store notes and other office materials. Primarily used by older people.

Generally shown as a brown case with a handle on top, and a silver or gold colored clasp on the front. Facebook shows two leather straps on the front.

A retail bank branch, where people can perform money-related tasks. Also a common location to find an ATM.

This emoji came to also mean "slacking off" or evading responsibility in Japan, due to the BK letters being associated with the slang term bakkureru.

The Tokyo Tower is the second-tallest building in Japan, located in Minato, Tokyo.

Built in 1957, the design of the Tokyo Tower  was inspired by the Eiffel Tower in Paris, France and may be confused for it due to the small size of the emoji. A previous Samsung design also added to this confusion as it was colored grey instead of red and white.

A car being shown from the front. The windscreen and hood (bonnet in British English) of the car can be seen facing forward.

This car shows in red or blue on most platforms. It was previously silver on Android.
A tractor, may be used by a farmer or other occupation on the land.

An elephant, the largest land animal on Earth, with a long trunk and, often, tusks. Generally depicted in gray in full profile on all fours facing left, with tusks and prominent ears, as an African (vs. Asian) elephant.

Google and Facebook’s elephants were previously blue in color. Samsung’s design previously featured a cartoon-styled elephant with a red blanket on its back and blowing a red heart from its trunk.

Because the elephant is a symbol of the Republican Party of the United States, it may be used in political contexts

A hippopotamus, a squat water mammal with huge jaws. Generally depicted in gray or tan in full profile facing left.

Google’s design used to feature a purple, cartoon-styled hippopotamus face. Facebook’s hippopotamus is opening massive jaws, revealing tusks.

A swan, a waterbird with white feathers and a long neck. Depicted in full profile facing left, with a curving neck, orange bill, black eye marking, and wings and legs tucked in, as if gliding in water.

May be used to represent a goose or, metaphorically, love, grace, and beauty.

An owl, the hooting, large-eyed bird. Depicted as a brown owl with its head facing forward. Shown with large, round, gold-rimmed eyes, talons, tucked wings, and horn-like tufts of feathers. May be used to represent wisdom.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

Once popularly used in connection with the hip-hop artist Drake.

Microsoft’s owl previously resembled a barn owl, Samsung’s was purple.

A brown or gray dodo shown in full profile. Generally depicted with a curved yellow beak, small wings, a fluffy white tail, yellow or orange feet, and black talons.

May be used to represent dodos or the concept of being extinct.

A single feather slanted to one side. On most platforms it's light brown with a dark brown barred or striped pattern. Can be used to talk about feathers or birds, or to represent something that is lightweight, fluffy, or soft.

A flamingo, a waterbird with pink feathers and long neck and legs. Depicted as a flamingo in full profile facing left, standing on one leg, usually with a long, black beak.

May be used to represent summer fun or as a pink accent color.

A peacock, the male bird that displays a large, fan-like, iridescent tale. Depicted facing forward standing on its legs, with a blue body and green tail feathers outspread.

Sometimes used to suggest something is beautiful or proud. Also sometimes used to accent a peacock-like color or pattern.

A parrot, a brightly colored bird known for its ability to mimic speech. Depicted in full profile facing left. Resembles a green lovebird with red and yellow wings on some platforms and a scarlet macaw with blue and yellow wings on others.

Can be used to represent various parrots or birds in general. May also be used to talk about mimicking.

Facebook’s parrot is orange with blue-tipped wings. Google's parrot was previously a scarlet macaw perched on a branch.

A single white wing with feathers.

Can be used to talk about flying, both literally and metaphorical. May be used in phrases such as when pigs fly or time flies. May also be used to talk about angels or to say that someone or something is angelic.

A bird with black feathers, shown either standing in full profile or as a bird head. Can be used to represent various black-feathered birds, such as crows, ravens, blackbirds, and more.

Black-feathered birds have been associated with magic and the occult across many global cultures, often as an omen of bad tidings.

Frequently associated with the Baltimore Ravens, an American football team.

A white goose in full profile.

Can be used to talk about the actual animal. Can also be used in the context of idioms including silly goose, wild goose chase, or what's good for the goose is good for the gander. Can also be used to talk about goosebumps or goose pimples.

Might be used in reference to the children's game duck duck goose.
A phoenix, a mythical immortal bird with flame-like feathers found in the folklore of many global cultures. Often used to symbolize renewal or rebirth.

May be used to talk about actual nests or birds. May also be used to talk about home in general or to represent phrases like nest egg or empty nest.

🪺 Nest with Eggs was approved at the same time and may be used along with Empty Nest.

A bird's nest with eggs inside.

May be used to talk about actual nests or birds. May also be used to talk about home in general or to represent phrases like nest egg or empty nest.

🪹 Empty Nest was approved at the same time as Nest with Eggs.

The face of a frog, the hopping amphibian. Generally depicted as a friendly, cartoon-styled, light-green frog looking straight ahead, with large eyes, slightly open mouth, and nostrils.

Popularly paired with ☕ Hot Beverage to represent the But That’s None of My Business meme (used for gossip or sarcasm) or Pepe the Frog (associated with trolling and the alt-right).

Facebook’s design previously resembled Kermit the Frog.

A crocodile, a stealthy reptile with massive jaws. Generally depicted as a light-green crocodile on all fours, with its long tail curving down to its toothed jaws, facing left.

May resemble and be used for an alligator.

Facebook's crocodile is opening its jaws. Samsung’s design previously resembled a kind of cartoon dinosaur.

A turtle, a slow-moving reptile with a shell. Depicted as a light-green turtle in full profile on all fours facing left, with a long neck and green, textured shell.

May be used to represent a tortoise and various senses of slow.

WhatsApp’s turtle has light-brown skin, Facebook’s a yellow-rimmed shell.

A lizard, a scaly reptile with a long tail. Depicted as a light-green lizard on all fours from above, generally looking left with large eyes, a lightly textured or colored back, and toes outspread, as a gecko.

May be used for a variety of wild and pet lizards.

Google’s lizard was previously brown.

A snake, a slithering reptile without limbs. Generally depicted as a yellowish-green snake facing left, with a long, coiled body and flicking a red, forked tongue.

May be used for various metaphorical senses of snake.

One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac. May also be used in association with ⛎ Ophiuchus, the Serpent-Bearer, sometimes considered a 13th sign of the Western zodiac.

Samsung’s snake was previously facing forward.

The face of a dragon, a mythical creature resembling a giant reptile found in the folklore of many cultures. Depicted as a green, Chinese-styled dragon looking straight ahead or facing left. Often shown with huge nostrils, baring large teeth and a red tongue, with antler-like structures on its head, whisker-like tendrils by its nostrils, and a green or yellow mane.

See also 🐉 Dragon. One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac. Commonly used on Chinese New Year and St. George's Day. Also used for various medieval and fantasy content.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

Microsoft's dragon face was previously red and looking straight ahead. Samsung's dragon face previously resembled a red, friendly, cartoon-styled imp with horns.

A dragon, a mythical creature resembling a giant reptile found in the folklore of many cultures. Depicted as a green, Chinese-styled dragon in full profile facing left. Generally shown with a curling, snake-like body, clawed feet, yellowish scales on its back, horn-like structures on its head, and whisker-like tendrils by its nostrils.

See also 🐲 Dragon Face. One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac. Commonly used on Chinese New Year and St. George's Day. Also used for various medieval and fantasy content.

Apple's dragon is holding a glowing blue orb, as a 🔮 Crystal Ball. Facebook's dragon is bluish in color. Microsoft's dragon was previously red, Samsung's a more cartoon-styled, baby dragon holding a blue orb.

A sauropod, a massive, plant-eating dinosaur with a long neck and tail. Depicted as a blue, gray, or green sauropod, as a brachiosaurus, apatosaurus/brontosaurus, or diplodocus. Shown in full profile on all fours facing left.

May be used to represent various dinosaurs. See also 🦖 T-Rex.

May also be used to call a person a dinosaur, i.e. imply that they are old-fashioned or out-of-touch with modern sentiments.

Apple, Google and Samsung's sauropods resemble a brachiosaurus. Samsung’s sauropod was previously green, Facebook’s previously displayed only a green head.

A Tyrannosaurus rex, a massive, meat-eating dinosaur with huge jaws, tiny arms, and a long tail. Depicted as a green tyrannosaur standing on its hind lefts facing left, often with a textured back, sharp teeth, and clawed toes.

May be used to represent various dinosaurs, including raptors. See also 🦕 Sauropod.

May also be used to call a person a dinosaur, i.e. imply that they are old-fashioned or out-of-touch with modern sentiments.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

Google’s T-rex used to look somewhat like a velociraptor, though the design has since changed. Samsung’s T-Rex was previously red, Microsoft's brown, and Facebook’s only a green head with open jaws.

A friendly, cartoon-styled whale, shown spouting water from its blowhole. Generally depicted as a light-blue whale in full profile facing left, with a round body and white underside, its tail held upright.

Often used with an affectionate tone. Not to be confused with the more lifelike 🐋 Whale, though their applications may overlap.

WhatsApp’s whale is gray, as Microsoft and Facebook’s whales previously were. Twitter’s whale was previously purple.

A whale, the massive marine mammal. Generally depicted as a light-blue whale in full profile facing left, with its tail curving down towards is huge mouth. Shown with a white, textured underside, as a humpback or blue whale.

Not to be confused with the more cartoon-styled 🐳 Spouting Whale, though their applications may overlap.

Apple and Google's whales have slightly open mouths, revealing baleen.

A dolphin, a sleek marine mammal known to be social and intelligent. Generally depicted as a light-blue dolphin with a white belly in full profile facing left, its short snout curving down to a prominent dorsal fin and tail, as a bottlenose dolphin leaping in the air.

May be used for various content concerning swimming, oceans, beaches, and summer fun. Not be confused with 🦈 Shark.

Frequently associated with the Miami Dolphins, an American football team.

WhatsApp and Facebook’s dolphins are gray, as Microsoft and Samsung’s previously were.
An orca, also known as a “killer whale”.

A gray seal with dark eyes and a dark nose. Most platforms feature a design with whiskers.

Can be used to talk about seals, marine life, or cute animals in general. May also be used in phrases with 'sealed' as in sealed with a kiss, my lips are sealed, seal of approval, or signed, sealed, and delivered.

A common fish, as swims in the water. Depicted as a generic, light-blue fish, often with a white underside, in full profile facing left, with fins and prominent gill cover.

May be used to represent a variety of other fish (freshwater or saltwater), fishing, metaphorical senses of fish, and fish as food, as consumed in the form of 🍣 Sushi. May be used to represent ♓ Pisces, the Fish, in the Western zodiac.

Not to be confused with 🐠 Tropical Fish or 🐡 Blowfish, though their applications may overlap. Vendors implement a similar design to the fish caught on the 🎣 Fishing Pole.

Microsoft’s fish was previously yellow.

A tropical fish, as swims in the warm waters of a coral reef or is kept as a pet in an aquarium. Depicted as a brightly colored fish in full profile facing left, with slender fins. Often shown as a blue-and-yellow fish with stripes, as an angelfish.

May be used to represent a variety of fish (saltwater or freshwater), fishing, metaphorical senses of fish, and fish as food, as consumed in the form of 🍣 Sushi. Not to be confused with 🐟 Fish or 🐡 Blowfish, though their applications may overlap. See also 🎣 Fishing Pole.

Google and Facebook’s fish previously resembled a goldfish, while Samsung’s was black and white. Microsoft’s fish was previously orange with white stripes, and yellow and blue before that.

A blowfish (puffer), which puffs up and becomes spiky when alarmed. Depicted as an orange or brown blowfish in full profile facing left, with small fins, a white underside, and a round, spiky body, as if inflated.

Called fugu in Japan, where it’s consumed as a delicacy.

May be to represent a variety of fish (saltwater or freshwater), fishing, metaphorical senses of fish, and fish as food, as consumed in the form of 🍣 Sushi. Not to be confused with 🐟 Fish or 🐠 Tropical Fish, though their applications may overlap. See also 🎣 Fishing Pole.

Google’s blowfish was previously blue, Microsoft’s yellow, and Facebook’s white.

A shark, a large, stealthy fish with many teeth.

Generally depicted as a gray shark in full profile facing left, as a tiger, bull, or great white shark hunting in the water. Shown with a white underside and three gills, its pointed nose and teeth-lined mouth curving down to a sharp dorsal fin and long, pointed tail.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

Not to be confused with 🐬 Dolphin.

An octopus, a sea animal with eight legs, known to change color and release ink. Generally depicted as a pink or orange octopus facing forward, with a large, round head, prominent eyes, and its tentacle-like arms raised at its sides. Platforms vary in the number of arms shown, ranging from four to the full eight, with several designs featuring suckers on them.

Not to be confused with 🦑 Squid, though their applications may overlap.

Available as an Apple Animoji.

Twitter’s octopus is purple. Apple’s has a friendly, cartoon-styled appearance. Google and Samsung’s octopuses previously looked surprised, while Microsoft's suggested an 👾 Alien Monster.

A seashell, as found at the beach. Generally depicted as an empty, spiraling, white seashell, as grown by a sea snail or home to a hermit crab. Positioned at various angles across platforms.

Often used for various content concerning beaches, ocean and ocean life, and summer fun. May also be used in reference to the vagina.

Apple’s design previously resembled a clam shell, Microsoft’s a snail shell. Google’s was previously blue.

Coral as found in a reef, of varying shapes and colors. Sometimes used as a symbol of climate change due to coral bleaching.

Depending on the emoji keyboard being used, this emoji may appear among either animal or plant emojis. This variation notably resulted in criticism from social media users following the release of iOS 15.4, as corals are animals, not plants.
A brightly colored jellyfish with a domed bell and dangling tentacles.

A crab, a squat crustacean with pincers. Depicted as a reddish-orange crab (as cooked) shown from above, with a round, shelled body, shorted, tentacle-like eyes, and ten legs, the top two of which are large pincers.

May be used to represent crab as food or metaphorical senses of crab (e.g., crabby). Often used to represent ♋ Cancer, the Crab, in the Western zodiac.

Not to be confused with 🦞 Lobster.

Facebook’s pincers have black tips, as do Huawei's.

A lobster, a large crustacean with a prominent tail and pincers. Depicted as a reddish-orange lobster (as cooked) from above, with a long body and tail, short, tentacle-like eyes, and ten legs, the top of which are very large pincers.

Often used to represent lobster as food as well as in connection to the US state of Maine.

In its release year of 2018, Emojipedia’s original sample image was criticized as anatomically incorrect but was shortly after resolved. That year, the transgender community embraced the lobster as a symbol for their efforts for Transgender Flag emoji.

Samsung, WhatsApp, and Facebook’s lobsters are depicted at an angle.

A shrimp (prawn), a small crustacean with a long tail. Generally depicted as a reddish-orange shrimp (as cooked) in full profile facing left, with tiny eyes, many limbs, and its long antennae curling back as its long tail curls in.

May be consumed in the form of 🍤 Fried Shrimp or 🥘 Shallow Pan of Food. Often used to represent seafood.

The antennae of Apple’s shrimp curls under its body. The body of Facebook’s shrimp is straight. Google and Samsung’s shrimp previously faced right.

A squid, an octopus-like sea animal with ten arms. Generally depicted as a pinkish-orange giant squid, facing forward or angled to the left, with a slender, arrow-like body, small eyes, and two, long arms raised up at its sides. Platforms generally depict six arms.

Occasionally used to represent squid as a food item. Not to be confused with 🐙 Octopus, though their applications may overlap.

Microsoft, WhatsApp and Twitter’s squid designs are facing forward, as was a previous Google design. Samsung’s squid was previously gray.
Half of an opened oyster shell with gray, pink, or orange flesh inside. Many platforms also include a pearl in the shell.

A snail, a slow-moving, snail-like mollusk in a spiraling shell. Generally depicted as a brown snail in full profile facing left or right, with a brown, textured shell and tentacle-like eyes.

May be used to represent a slug and various senses of slow.

Twitter’s snail has a purple body and yellow shell. Microsoft’s snail previously had a green body.

A butterfly, a beautiful winged insect whose larva is a caterpillar. Depicted with its wings outspread, as a blue-and-black morpho butterfly or orange-and-black monarch butterfly.

May be used to represent a moth and ideas of beauty and happiness.

Since December 2023 this emoji has been used to reference the social media platform Bluesky, due to the platform's logo being a blue butterfly.

Samsung’s butterfly previously resembled a monarch.

A bug, or insect, generally depicted as a caterpillar, which becomes a 🦋 Butterfly. Shown in full profile facing left, inching up on the back of its green, segmented, and textured body. Often featuring black stripes or yellow dots and tentacles on its head.

May be used to represent various insects, worms, and related animals. May also be used for metaphorical senses of bug.

Twitter’s bug is purple. Apple’s bug is hairy with a red head and legs and black stripes on its body. Facebook’s bug also has a yellowish-orange head. Google and Microsoft’s bugs previously resembled an orange centipede or millipede, and Samsung’s had a cartoon-styled face with a purple nose.

An ant, a small, industrious insect that lives in a colony. Depicted as a black or red ant in full profile on its six legs facing left, with a prominent abdomen and antennae.

May be used to represent various insects or other bugs.

Facebook’s ant is red, as was a previous Microsoft design. Google’s ant was previously blue, Facebook’s black.

A honey bee, a busy, flying insect that lives in a hive and makes honey. Depicted as a black-and-yellow bee with clear or white wings and a stinger. Variously facing left in full profile or shown from above.

May be used to represent various types of bees (e.g., bumblebee) and wasps (e.g., hornets, yellow jackets). May also be used to accent black-and-yellow colors or patterns. Popularly used in connection with singer and superstar Beyoncé (nicknamed Queen Bey) or for metaphorical queen bees. Can also be used to refer to the city of Manchester in the United Kingdom, as the worker bee is the symbol of the city.

A green or brown beetle shown with antennae and six legs. Can be used to talk about beetles, bugs, or insects in general.

Not to be confused with 🐞 Lady Beetle, 🪳 Cockroach, 🐛 Bug, 🐜 Ant or other emoji representations of insects.

A ladybug (ladybird, lady beetle), a beetle with a round, red shell with black spots. Generally depicted as a seven- or nine-spotted ladybug shown from above on its six legs, with antennae and its distinctively red-and-black, halved shell.

May be used a symbol of good luck.

Facebook’s ladybug is shown on its legs facing forward.

A cricket, a hopping insect that makes a chirping sound. Depicted as a brown or green cricket in full profile on its six legs facing left, with long antennae and large, bent back legs.

May resemble or be used to represent a grasshopper (including locusts) and other bugs. May also be used to represent metaphorical crickets, or "silence," as of a disapproving or uninterested audience.

Not to be confused with 🏏 Cricket Game, the sport.

Google's cricket was previously green.

A brown cockroach shown with antennae, six legs, and two sensory pads at its rear called cerci.

Can be used to talk about cockroaches or insects in general. May also be used metaphorically as an insult to call a person a pest, an annoyance, or to suggest they are subhuman.

A spider, an eight-legged arachnid that spins a web. Depicted as a common black spider, as a house spider or funnel-web spider, often shown from above with its large abdomen oriented at the bottom.

See also 🕸 Spider Web. Commonly used during Halloween and to represent the superhero Spider-Man.

Facebook’s spider is facing left. Google's spider was previously upside down, suspended from a thread, though now is facing left. Microsoft’s spider was previously a black widow, while Samsung’s was brown.

A classic spider web (cobweb), as spun by a 🕷 Spider to catch prey. Depicted as a white, symmetrical, wheel-shaped web, as an orb web, with six or eight equal sectors.

Commonly used during Halloween, to represent the superhero Spider-Man, or for a metaphorical web, net, or network. Not to be confused with ❄ Snowflake.

A scorpion, an arachnid with lobster-like pincers and a stinging tail. Depicted as a light-brown scorpion from above, often facing left, with its pincers and curving stinger raised. Shown with six or, accurately, eight legs in addition to its pincers.

Often used to represent ♏ Scorpio in the Western zodiac.

WhatsApp’s scorpion is reddish in color.

A mosquito, a type of bloodsucking fly. Depicted as a brown or black mosquito on its six, long legs, with wings, long abdomen, and needle-like mouth. Variously shown from above or facing left.

May be used to represent various insects, other bugs and bug bites, and insect-borne diseases (e.g., malaria). May also be used for metaphorical pests.

Facebook’s mosquito has a red abdomen, as if filled with blood.

A fly with a dark or iridescent green body, six legs, and two translucent wings. On most platforms, its eyes are red.

Can be used to talk about the insect or flight in general. May also be used metaphorically as an adjective meaning "cool."

A pink or brown worm. Most platforms have more realistic designs, though Google and Samsung feature cartoony worms who are smiling sweetly.

Can be used to talk about worms or disease spread by worms. Can also be used to refer to a deceitful person. May be used to in reference to the dance move 'the worm.'

A microbe, as a bacterium grown in a 🧫 Petri Dish or observed under a 🔬 Microscope. Generally depicted as a squiggly, single-celled microorganism with prominent cilia. Color, shape, and position vary across platforms. Commonly used to represent bacteria, viruses, and germs and disease more generally.

In 2020, this emoji became primarily used in reference to Coronavirus / COVID-19.

Apple's version of this emoji most closely represents a virus, while others from Samsung, Microsoft and Twitter appear as bright green bacteria. Other versions of this emoji also appear mainly as bacteria: Facebook's is indigo, and WhatsApp’s purple. Google’s design previously displayed five microbes in different, bright colors.

A bouquet of brightly colored flowers. Generally depicted as a collection of pink and yellow flowers with green stems tied together. Positioned at various angles across platforms.

Commonly used for Valentine’s Day, Mother’s Day, and other special occasions. May also be more generally used to express such sentiments as love, appreciation, and happiness.

Google’s flowers were previously all yellow, Microsoft’s roses, and Samsung’s pink and white.

The pink flower of a cherry blossom tree. Depicted as a single, light-pink cherry blossom with five, notched petals and red-tipped stamens in a yellow or white center.

A traditional symbol in Japan, where the flower is called sakura and celebrated in annual viewings.

Commonly used for Valentine’s Day, Mother’s Day, and other special occasions. May be more generally used to express such ideas as love and beauty. Also used as a pink accent color.

Not to be confused with 💮 White Flower and 🌺 Hibiscus, though their applications may overlap.

A stylized white flower. Generally depicted as a rosette-shaped cherry blossom in pink or red outline, often with a white fill.

Apple, Microsoft, WhatsApp, and Facebook's designs feature Japanese characters roughly translating to very well done, used by teachers as a stamp for students who did exceptional work, often accompanied by a score in red.
